v: Evidence from self-report studies supports the hypothesis that men favor children who are perceived as facially resembling them (Burch & Gallup, 2000; Volk & Quinsey, 2002). Platek, Burch, Panyavin, Wasserman, and Gallup (2002) and Platek et al. (2003) provided some of the first experimental evidence consistent with the hypothesis that men are more sensitive than women are to children's resemblance to self, reporting a series of results based on reactions to images of child faces that were digitally manipulated to resemble the experimental participants.
